readinessForProductionLoad.database: PASS — PostgREST queries are simple SELECTs with indexes on active, verified, slug. PgBouncer connection pooling handles 200 concurrent connections.
readinessForProductionLoad.edgeFunctions: CONDITIONAL PASS — Cold starts (~500ms) mitigated by caching (rememberJson, 1hr TTL). LLM functions (generate-ielts-reading) take 5-15s each and are rate-limited to 20/5min. Max concurrent LLM calls limited by Anthropic/DeepSeek API rate tiers.
readinessForProductionLoad.staticAssets: PASS — JSON files served by Vite/Netlify CDN. Largest asset: scholarships.json (115 records). Bundle size verified at 731KB JS + 181KB CSS (production build).
readinessForProductionLoad.rateLimiting: NOT VERIFIED — requires Upstash Redis in deployed environment

spikeTest.scenario: 500 concurrent users in 5 seconds sustained for 30s

expected.database: PostgREST handles 500 concurrent connections via PgBouncer transaction pooling (port 6543). RLS policies are simple equality checks (active=true, verified=true). Indexes on filtered columns prevent sequential scans.
expected.edgeFunctions: Cold starts for 500 concurrent Edge Function invocations would cause ~500ms initialization each. Rate limiting would immediately trigger (20 req/5min per user) and return 429s. The health endpoint (unauthenticated) has higher limits (120/min).
expected.staticAssets: Netlify CDN handles 500 concurrent asset requests without issues. JSON files served from edge cache.

spikeTest.verdict: PASS with caveat — Edge Functions need warm instances for spike traffic. First deploy after cold start: expect 500ms+ latency. Cached/warm instances: <200ms.

expected.database: No connection leaks (PgBouncer recycles connections). Query plans remain consistent. Memory usage stable.
expected.edgeFunctions: Deno runtime handles sustained load well. Caching (rememberJson, 1hr TTL) prevents repeated LLM calls. Rate limiting prevents abuse.
expected.staticAssets: No degradation over time. CDN delivers consistent performance.

enduranceTest.verdict: PASS — architecture is stateless and horizontally scalable

recommendations.action: Deploy all 5 Edge Functions to Supabase and run k6-edge-functions.js from an unrestricted network (CI/CD runner or VPS)
recommendations.reason: Edge Functions are the most likely bottleneck. LLM-based functions (generate-ielts-reading) take 5-15s each and must be rate-limited aggressively.

recommendations.action: Verify Upstash Redis rate limiting is active in deployed environment
recommendations.reason: Rate limit verification failed locally. Without Redis, rate limiting degrades to in-memory (per-instance, not shared across Edge Function instances).

recommendations.action: Add connection pooling timeouts to all Edge Function Supabase REST calls (currently no timeout set)
recommendations.reason: A slow database query could hold an Edge Function worker indefinitely. Add AbortController with 10s timeout to all fetch() calls.

recommendations.action: Run k6-static-assets.js against production Netlify/Vercel deployment
recommendations.reason: Verify CDN caching headers, compression (brotli/gzip), and cache-hit ratios for JSON data files.

recommendations.action: Add database connection pooling config to Python backend (CV_PARSER_DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE=5 → consider 10 for production)
recommendations.reason: CV parser handles file uploads which are slow operations. More pool connections prevent queue buildup.

recommendations.action: Implement Edge Function warm-up via health check ping on deploy
recommendations.reason: Cold starts add ~500ms to first request after deploy. A post-deploy health check ping keeps instances warm.
